abstract: [Frontiers in medicine] Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of healthcare, particularly in rheumatology, where clinicians must integrate complex clinical, laboratory, and imaging data. Physicians' perceptions of AI may substantially influence the extent to which it is implemented responsibly in routine clinical practice. This study aimed to assess the attitudes of practicing rheumatologists in Iraq toward artificial intelligence and to examine their association with demographic and professional characteristics. A four-month web-based cross-sectional survey was conducted from October 2025 to January 2026. A questionnaire adapted from previous studies was refined through expert review and pilot testing before distribution. The questionnaire comprised demographic information, attitude statements measured on a five-point Likert scale, and items assessing general perceptions of artificial intelligence. Composite attitude scores were categorized using modified Bloom's cutoff criteria. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS and R. A total of 162 complete responses were collected. Most respondents were aged 35-44 years (42.0%), male (56.8%), and specialists (67.9%). Overall, 61.7% reported familiarity with AI and 69.1% had already used AI in rheumatology practice. Most participants 56.8% exhibited a poor attitude, 32.1% a moderate attitude, and 11.1% a good attitude toward AI. Bivariate analysis identified familiarity with AI ( p = 0.003 ) and involvement in research ( p = 0.009 ) as significantly associated with more favorable attitudes. Iraqi rheumatologists demonstrate cautious engagement with artificial intelligence, with the majority displaying poor-to-moderate overall attitude scores on the standardized composite scale. Greater familiarity with AI and research involvement were associated with more favorable attitudes, highlighting the importance of targeted digital literacy and specialty-specific education to support effective AI adoption in clinical practice.

abstract: [Frontiers in digital health] Building on a previous Wales-wide survey, this study aimed to provide more in-depth exploration of the barriers and facilitators to healthcare artificial intelligence adoption in Wales. The study aimed to explore these barriers and facilitators among various social groups, to inform policy development in Wales. Four focus groups were conducted with a group of members of the public and a group of healthcare professionals (both groups recruited from a previous survey), as well as a group Sixth Form students and a group of retired adults. Inductive thematic analysis was used to generate themes and to compare the issues raised by the various groups. Contiguity-based analysis was undertaken to underscore how themes related with each other. A total of 21 individuals participated in the focus groups (healthcare professionals=6, members of the public=6, sixth-form students=5, retirees=4). Seven thematic networks were identified. Across groups, seven themes were identified in the healthcare professional group, six in the general members of the public group, seven in the sixth form student group, and seven in the retiree group. All groups voiced concerns about data privacy and highlighted the importance of human oversight of AI and human contact during the clinical encounter as they expressed more trust in human practitioners. There were though differences between groups, such as greater trust in black-box systems by healthcare professionals, and between individual participants in regard to trust in private organisations developing AI for healthcare organisations. All groups were concerned with information security and expressed a preference for human contact during the clinical encounter and a human-in-the-loop approach. There were differences between the groups, such as in attitudes towards black-box AI technologies and trust in clinicians. No additional barriers or facilitators were identified for proxy consent.
zh_abstract: [Frontiers in digital health] 在先前一项威尔士全境调查的基础上，本研究旨在更深入地探讨威尔士医疗保健人工智能采用的障碍与促进因素。本研究旨在探讨不同社会群体中的这些障碍与促进因素，以为威尔士政策制定提供信息。研究开展了四个焦点小组，分别包括一组公众成员和一组医疗保健专业人员（两组均从先前调查中招募），以及一组六年级学生（Sixth Form students）和一组退休成年人。采用归纳性主题分析生成主题，并比较不同群体提出的问题。进行了基于邻接性的分析，以强调各主题之间如何相互关联。共有21名个体参加焦点小组（医疗保健专业人员=6，公众成员=6，六年级学生=5，退休人员=4）。识别出七个主题网络。跨群体来看，医疗保健专业人员组识别出七个主题，普通公众组六个，六年级学生组七个，退休人员组七个。所有群体都对数据隐私表示担忧，并强调人工智能的人类监督以及临床接触期间人际接触的重要性，因为他们对人类从业者表达了更多信任。不过群体之间存在差异，例如医疗保健专业人员对黑箱系统信任度更高，以及个体参与者之间在对为医疗保健组织开发人工智能的私营组织的信任方面存在差异。所有群体都关注信息安全，并表示偏好临床接触期间的人际接触和“人在环路”（human-in-the-loop）方法。群体之间存在差异，例如对黑箱人工智能技术的态度以及对临床医生的信任。对于代理同意（proxy consent），未识别出额外的障碍或促进因素。
